messages:
Maria R.: Quick flag question — we've had a few asks to let clients opt-in to A/B routing. Thinking we should only accept client-side variant headers when project opt-in is enabled. Example header ideas: `x-redwood-variant: canary-v2` or `x-redwood-optin: true`. Thoughts?
Samir K.: I like separating concerns: `x-redwood-variant` for tracing/routing intent and `x-redwood-optin` as a feature toggle. Also we need server-side checks so clients can't force traffic.
Lee P.: Absolutely. Server guard must verify project-level opt-in + maybe allowlist of SDK keys. Otherwise any external caller could put a variant header.
Maria R.: For Console UX: show a per-project toggle "Allow client-specified variants" + an allowlist of SDK IDs / client IDs. @console-ux can you mock a small control?
console-ux: Yep. Proposal: one card under Routing -> "Client Routing" with Toggle, Allowlist, and a small audit log. Add a red warning copy: "Only enable if you trust your clients".
Samir K.: Implementation note: routing pipeline should treat header only if (1) project opt-in true, (2) client id in allowlist OR sdk-registered, (3) header not exceeding sample rate guard. Also emit metrics for accept/reject.
Lee P.: HMAC-signed header would be ideal for integrity, but heavy for some clients. Alternative: require SDK to register and keep server-side mapping of sdk-id -> secret; accept header only if sdk-id present and matches registration.
Maria R.: Good call. For SDKs we'll add an explicit opt-in API: `Redwood.configure({ clientRouting: true })` that registers the sdk-id with server. Only then SDK sends `x-redwood-sdk-id` + `x-redwood-variant`.
Samir K.: So headers we expect: `x-redwood-sdk-id: sdk_abc123` and `x-redwood-variant: canary-v2`. Server checks registration + project toggle + per-variant quota. If any check fails we ignore header and route normally.
Maria R.: Telemetry: emit `redwood.client.header.accepted` and `redwood.client.header.rejected` with tags {project, variant, reason}. Also log a tiny sampled trace for rejections so we can surface common failure reasons in console.
console-ux: On dashboard we can show trend: % accepted vs rejected, top rejection reasons, and a quick link to enable/disable. Also surface when a variant spike comes from clients vs server rollouts.
Lee P.: Add rollout guard: console toggle should be gated behind a canary rollout at infra level (10% initially) and we should auto-disable if rejection-rate > 5% or error-rate increases.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: feature flag `client-header-optin` -> canary -> 10% -> scheduled 2026-03-19T02:00Z.
Samir K.: I'll draft a short RFC with sequence: Console UX -> server validation -> SDK API -> telemetry -> canary rollout -> observability. Will include sample code for header parsing and a fallback path.
Maria R.: Perfect. Small docs blurb for SDKs: "SDKs will only send variant headers after explicit opt-in via the Redwood Console or SDK API call; otherwise headers are ignored." Can someone paste that into the SDK release notes?
Samir K.: Will do in the SDK changelog. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
